queries.hook: I have to make a big decision. Inside, I keep going over it again and again, and I don't know how to carry it.
queries.diagnose: Confusion comes when duties pull in different directions and fear clouds which one is truly yours.
queries.steady: Your own duty, done imperfectly, is better than another's; when the mind clears, the right step becomes plain.
queries.act: Ask what is right, not what is easy; choose your own duty with a clear mind and carry it out without fear.
queries.story: A story of a seeker whose mind will not settle, facing torn between duties.

hook.speaker: Arjuna
hook.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
hook.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचअयतिः श्रद्धयोपेतो योगाच्चलितमानसः । अप्राप्य योगसंसिद्धिं कां गतिं कृष्ण गच्छति ॥
hook.line: What happens to someone who believes, tries, slips, and doesn't make it to the end?
hook.translation: Arjuna said: One who has faith but does not strive enough, whose mind falls away from yoga before reaching perfection, what end does he come to, Krishna?
hook.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

prasang.title: What becomes of one who falls from yoga
prasang.summary: Arjuna fears that one who falls short is lost like a torn cloud. Krishna promises that no one who does good comes to ruin; past effort carries forward and they strive again.
prasang.lesson: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

hook.for_you: You keep walking the same ground, and a verse is chosen to sit with you.
hook.first_line: You keep walking the same ground, and a verse is chosen to sit with you.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna confesses the mind is as hard to hold as the wind; Krishna answers.
alternates.sanskrit: अर्जुन उवाचयोऽयं योगस्त्वया प्रोक्तः साम्येन मधुसूदन । एतस्याहं न पश्यामि चञ्चलत्वात् स्थितिं स्थिराम् ॥
alternates.line: This calm you describe, Krishna, I can't see it lasting. My mind is too restless.
alternates.translation: Arjuna said: This yoga of evenness that you have taught, Madhusudana, I do not see how it can last, because of restlessness.
alternates.why: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

prasang.title: Mastering the mind
prasang.summary: Arjuna says the mind is restless, stormy and stubborn. Krishna agrees, and says practice and letting go can train it.
prasang.lesson: The mind is hard to hold, but practice and letting go train it.

alternates.speaker: Arjuna
alternates.setting: Arjuna asks what becomes of someone who tries and fails; Krishna reassures him.
alternates.sanskrit: कच्चिन्नोभयविभ्रष्टश्छिन्नाभ्रमिव नश्यति । अप्रतिष्ठो महाबाहो विमूढो ब्रह्मणः पथि ॥
alternates.line: Fallen from both sides, does he scatter like a torn cloud, with nowhere to stand?
alternates.translation: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a broken cloud, without support, mighty-armed one, bewildered on the path to Brahman?
alternates.why: No sincere effort is wasted; you pick up where you left off.

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna explains the three qualities: clarity, restlessness and dullness.
verse.sanskrit: तमस्त्वज्ञानजं विद्धि मोहनं सर्वदेहिनाम् । प्रमादालस्यनिद्राभिस्तन्निबध्नाति भारत ॥
verse.line: Dullness, born of ignorance, ties you down through carelessness, laziness and too much sleep.
verse.translation: Know tamas to be born of ignorance, deluding all embodied beings. It binds through heedlessness, laziness and sleep, Bharata.
verse.why: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

prasang.title: Sattva, rajas, tamas: the three gunas
prasang.summary: Sattva binds through attachment to happiness and knowledge, rajas through craving and activity, tamas through laziness and sleep. Each shows itself in recognisable signs.
prasang.lesson: Notice which mood is running you: clarity, restlessness or dullness.

why: laziness and oversleep are explained as the binding of tamas, common to all embodied beings

verse.speaker: Krishna
verse.setting: Krishna to Arjuna on how to act without being chained to results.
verse.sanskrit: नेहाभिक्रमनाशोऽस्ति प्रत्यवायो न विद्यते । स्वल्पमप्यस्य धर्मस्य त्रायते महतो भयात् ॥
verse.line: No sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of it shields you from great fear.
verse.translation: On this path no effort is lost and no harm results. Even a little of this practice protects one from great fear.

words.en: here no stepping back, no destruction

verse.why: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

prasang.title: The yoga of action
prasang.summary: Krishna teaches the yoga of action: work wholeheartedly, give up clinging to outcomes, stay even in success and failure, and keep a single steady purpose.
prasang.lesson: Do the work fully; let go of owning the result.

verse.meaning: On this path, no beginning is lost and no harm results. Even a small amount of this practice protects from great fear. The tradition reads this as a path of action where every step forward counts, and even a little effort shields one from the fear of birth and death.
verse.for_you: You may feel stuck, but no sincere effort here is ever wasted. Even a little of this practice shields you from great fear.

why: answers the worry that an unfinished effort is a wasted one
Even a little of this path protects from great fear.

verse.speaker: Swami Vivekananda
verse.line: If you think yourselves weak, weak you will be; if you think yourselves strong, strong you will be;
verse.translation: Whatever you think, that you will be. If you think yourselves weak, weak you will be; if you think yourselves strong, strong you will be;
verse.why: Thoughts shape us, so teach yourself and your children strength.

prasang.title: 'Whatever you think, that you will be' (Jaffna, 1897)
prasang.summary: On his first tour after the West he summarises Vedanta for the Hindus of Jaffna. Thinking yourself weak makes you weak; children should be raised strong and told of the glory of the soul. Learn to serve before you lead.
prasang.lesson: Thoughts shape us, so teach yourself and your children strength.

verse.speaker: Vidura
verse.setting: Vidura counsels the sleepless King Dhritarashtra the night before the peace talks.
verse.sanskrit: निश्चित्य यः प्रक्रमते नान्तर्वसति कर्मणः / अवन्ध्यकालो वश्यात्मा स वै पण्डित उच्यते
verse.line: Decide, then begin. Don't stall halfway, don't waste time, and keep yourself steady.
verse.translation: One who begins only after deciding, does not stop halfway through the work, does not waste time and keeps himself in hand, is called wise.
verse.why: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

prasang.title: Vidura Niti: the wise and the fool
prasang.summary: Sleepless before the peace talks, King Dhritarashtra calls his half-brother Vidura for counsel. Vidura describes the marks of the wise and the fool, the faults that block progress, and the six joys of life.
prasang.lesson: Decide calmly, act steadily, forgive freely, and know what real happiness is made of.

why: Reflect fully, then decide and begin.
Nishchitya: begin from a settled decision

verse.speaker: Vasishtha
verse.setting: Vasishtha teaches the disheartened young Rama that effort, not fate, shapes his life.
verse.line: When your mind drifts to harmful things, steer it back to good ones. That's the whole teaching.
verse.translation: When the mind has sunk into bad things, bring it down into good ones with effort. That is the summary of all the scriptures.
verse.why: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

prasang.title: Vasishtha on self-effort: fate is only your past effort
prasang.summary: Vasishtha's first teaching to Rama is a long case for self-effort. What people call fate is simply the fruit of their own past effort, and present effort can overcome it, as the stronger of two rams wins. He also says not to torment yourself over what was beyond your power, and to steer your habits gently, like raising a child.
prasang.lesson: Your past effort shaped today; today's effort shapes tomorrow. Don't grieve what was never in your hands.

why: turn the mind back each time

story.title: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
story.summary: Bhartrihari praises learning as wealth no thief can take and speech as the one lasting ornament, then turns to good company and the three kinds of people who face obstacles. It ends with the 'sword's-edge vow' of the good.
story.lesson: What you learn and how you speak are the wealth no one can take from you.
story.teaser: Nitishatakam: In praise of learning and the learned
